Declaration of Ganga as National River 
 †*303. SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS : Will the Minister of WATER RESOURCES be pleased to 
state: 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 

 5
 (a) the steps being taken by Government to gi ve practical shape to the declaration of the 
Ganga as the National River; 
 (b) whether there is also a proposal  to stop some ongoing projects; and 
 (c) the measures being initiated to get pub lic cooperation in order to make this plan 
successful? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES  
(SHRI JAY PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) and (c) The Central Government has initiated an 
exercise for revamping the river conservation st rategy with an aim to promote a holistic and 
integrated approach of river basin planning. The process for setting up a River Basin Authority 
for River Ganga as an empowered, planning, impl ementing & monitoring Authority, vested with 
appropriate powers has been initiated in consulta tion with the Central Mi nistries and the State 
Governments. 
 (b) There is no proposal in the Ministry of Water Resources (MoWR) to stop ongoing 
projects. However, taking note of the concerns raised by some NGO’s regarding construction of 
Hydro Power Schemes on the river Ganga, the National Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC) 
has constituted a High Level Expert Group to examine the various issu es involved. The State 
Government of Uttarakhand has reportedly put on hold two hydro power projects namely 
Bhaironghati and Pala Maneri. 
Impact of terrorism on tourist arrival in India 
 *304. SHRI KAMAL AKHTAR: 
  DR. V. MAITREYAN: 
 Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 (a) what is the present level of  tourist arrivals in the country; 
 (b) what is the corresponding figures during the last year; 
 (c) whether the arrival of tourists has been se verely affected due to the security problem in 
the country on account of terrorists activities in the country; and 
 (d) what serious measures are being contempl ated to improve the security in the country 
to facilitate the tourist arrivals in the country? 
 THE MINISTER OF TOURISM (SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI): (a) to (d) The number of 
Foreign Tourist Arrivals (FTAs) in India dur ing January-November 2008 is estimated at 4.84 
million, which is higher than the FTAs of 4.48  million during January-November 2007. However, 
the growth rate in FTAs during January-November 2008 over the corresponding period of 2007 is 
only 8% as compared to growth rate of 14.8% in FTAs during January-November 2007 over the 
corresponding period of 2006. The lower growth rate in 2008 may be due to various reasons 
including the global financial meltdown and terrorist activities. To minimize the negative impact of 
recent terrorist attacks on tourism in the countr y, the Ministry of Tourism has undertaken the 
following confidence building measures:- 
  All States have been requested to beef up security measures in hotels and at tourist 
sites in their respective States;

media and travel trade to keep them updated on the ground situation in the country.

  SHRIMATI SHOBHANA BHARTIA: 
 Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
 (a) whether the public sector oil companies propose to upgrade thei r refineries and to 
equip them to process high sulphur crude oil to cut their import bill;

 (c) the existing refining capacity of each of th e refineries of the public sector oil companies 
and whether these capacities have been fully utilized in the last few years; and 
 (d) if so, the details thereof? 
 THE MINISTER OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS (SHRI MURLI DEORA): (a) and (b) 
The Public Sector Oil Companies are progressively increasing the processing of High Sulphur

(IOCL)-Barauni (part), IOCL-Gujarat (part) and Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited

 The Public Sector Oil Companies are regularly undertaking refinery upgradation projects for 
installation of high severity Fluidised Ca talytic Converter, Delayed Coker Unit, Coker 
Hydrotreater Unit, etc. to optimize high sulp hur crude oil processing  based on economics, 
pollution levels and product demand. Moreover, Fuel quality upgradation projects are presently 
being executed at the refineries of the Public Sector Oil Companies to meet the stringent 
Environmental Norms. The High Sulphur Crude proc essing capability is expected to go up after 
these projects commissioning. 
 (c) and (d) Most of the refineries (e xcept North Eastern refineries and CPCL-
Nagapattinam) have achieved improved capacity utilization over the years. Half of the number of 
refineries have achieved full capacity (100%) utiliz ation and overall industry average for the last

Pay disparity among Group ‘B’ Officers of various Ministries/Departments 
 *306. SHRI PRAVEEN RASHTRAPAL : Will th e PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
 (a) whether it is a fact that the Sixth Pay Co mmission has not looked into just demand of 
Group ‘B’ Officers of Information and Broadcasting (I&B) Ministry of granting them Group ‘A’ 
scale after completion of four years of service; 
 (b) whether it is also a fact that officers for the Railways, Accounts, Central Secretariat 
Service (CSS), Central Secretariat Stenogra phers Service (CSSS), Delhi, Andaman and 
Nicobar Islands Civil Service (DANICS) and Delh i, Andaman and Nicobar Islands Police Service 
(DANIPS) have been given better deal; and 
 (c) the steps taken by Government to improv e career prospects of Group ‘B’ Officers of 
I&B Ministry? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINI STRY OF FINANCE (SHRI PAWAN KUMAR 
BANSAL): (a) to (c)  Vide  para 7.22.4 of its Report, Sixth Central Pay Commission 
recommended that posts of Indian Information Se rvice Group ‘B’ of Ministry of Information & 
Broadcasting which were in the pre-revise d scales of Rs.5500-9000 and Rs.6500-10500 will 
come to lie in the same pay scale on account of restructuring of pay scales and functionally also 
they were similar. Therefore, these posts shou ld be merged. This recommendation of the Pay 
Commission regarding Group ‘B’ posts in Ministry of Information & Broadcasting has been 
accepted. For officers in the Railways, Accounts, Central Secretariat Service, Central Secretariat

the Pay Commission recommended replacement pa y band PB-2 with grade pay of Rs.5400, 
which was modified by Government to PB-3 with grade pay of Rs.5400.

  SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL: 
 Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
 (a) the present contribution of  producers in private sector oil Companies in meeting their 
social obligations; and 
 (b) whether Government has not made it obligatory by asking them to supply petroleum 
products to Government companies on Indian market prices before allowing them to export the

 THE MINISTER OF PETROLEUM AND NATURA L GAS (SHRI MURLI DEORA): (a) Private

Scarcity of water 
 †*308. SHRI BRIJ BHUSHAN TIWARI: 
  SHRI JANESHWAR MISHRA: 
 Will the Minister of WATER RESOURCES be pleased to state: 
 (a) whether Government is aware of scarcity of water in the country; 
 (b) if so, whether any initiative is being taken by Government for the distribution of water of 
Chenab, Kosi and Brahmaputra rivers under the international law; and 
 (c) if so, the details thereof? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES  
(SHRI JAY PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) the UNESCO Water Portal states that water 
scarcity has been defined as a situation where wate r availability in a country or a region is below 
1000 cubic metre per person per year. Considering the population of 2001 census, the per capita 
water availability in India works out to be 1820 Cu bic Metre. The per capita water availability is 
declining because of populati on growth. The National Commission on Integrated Water 
Resources Development has estimated that by the year 2050, when the population is expected 
to stabilize, the per capita water availability would be 1140 Cubic Metre. However, the per capita 
water availability varies considerably from one basin to another. 
 (b) and (c) Distribution of Chenab waters is  governed by the provisions of Indus Waters 
Treaty 1960 between India and Pakistan. Under the Treaty, India is under obligation to let flow all 
the Chenab waters and not permit any interfer ence with these waters, except for uses, as 
specified in the Treaty. A bilateral agreemen t on Kosi Barrage was signed between the 
Governments of India and Nepal in 1954, which wa s later revised in December 1966. There is no 
bilateral agreement with China for distribution of waters of Brahmaputra river. However, a Joint 
Expert Level Mechanism (ELM) has been set up under cooperation with China for cooperation 
for the supply of flood season hydrological data by China on river Brahmaputra. 
Job loss due to economic crisis 
 *309. MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
 (a) whether it is a fact that there is a like lihood that lakhs of employees may have to lose 
their jobs in the near future in view of the global economic crisis; 
 (b) if so, the details thereof; and 
 (c) the steps taken by Government in this regard? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINI STRY OF FINANCE (SHRI PAWAN KUMAR 
BANSAL): (a) and (b) Unlike the developed countries where job losses have been reported  
due to the global financial crisis, the impact has been limited in India as a large proportion  
of population is employed in the agriculture sector which has  not been  affected by the  crisis.  
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 

 11 
Besides, the services sector with a large share in  GDP has also been less affected. Even in the 
export sector which registered negative growth in October, 2008, the fall was mainly due to a 
spike in export growth in October, 2007 and is limited to some sectors only. While no 
comprehensive surveys have been conducted to estimate the likely job losses in India due to 
global economic crisis, a sample study of 121 export related companies (for the period  
August-October, 2008) by Department of Commerce  has indicated fall in jobs due to slowdown 
in some export sectors. A recent FICCI survey  indicates some downsizing in employment in 
coming months particularly in some export se ctors. Meanwhile, GDP growth is expected to 
moderate somewhat from very high growth rate in  the last 3 years, yet remain sufficiently high 
this year generating new employment opportunities. 
 (c) Government is concerned about the possible  impact of global financial crisis on the 
Indian economy, including employment, and severa l measures, financial and fiscal, have been 
taken. RBI’s measures to enhance liquidity in the market and the Government’s fiscal stimulus to 
help industrial growth and empolyment like reduct ion in three major ad valorem rates of Central 
Excise duty applicable to non-petroleum products  by 4 percentage points, withdrawai of export 
duty on iron ore (fines) and additional plan expenditure of upto Rs 20,000 crore in the current 
year would help address the problem. Further.  3.24 crore households have been provided 
employment under National Rural Employment Guarantee Act as on 15.12.2008 in the current 
financial year. 
Annual growth rate 
 †*310. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER SINGH MAJITHA: 
  DR. MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI: 
 Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
 (a) whether it is a fact that according to the mid term annual report of the Reserve Bank of 
India (RBI), the annual growth rate  in the current year is expected to be 7.5 per cent to 8 per 
cent and according to the Central Bank, the price index is expected to rise upto 7 per cent in the 
current year; 
 (b) if so, the details thereof; 
 (c) whether on the basis of the above figures, the growth rate in the country can be said to 
be satisfactory to the common man; and 
 (d) if not, what is Government’s reaction thereto? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINI STRY OF FINANCE (SHRI PAWAN KUMAR 
BANSAL): (a) and (b) The Reserv e Bank of India (RBI) has revised their GDP forecast for 
2008-09 to a range of 7.5-8.0 per cent. The growth has been revised downwards in view of the 
fact that the global down turn may be deeper and more protracted than expected earlier, with 
consequent adverse implication through trade and financial channels for emerging economies, 
including India, getting amplified. This could have  effects in the form of potential terms of Trade 
losses, erosion of export competitiveness and restricted external financing causing the growth in 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 

 12
Gross Domestic Product (GDP) at factor cost co nstant prices to decelerate to 7.8 per cent 
during April-September (2008-09) as against the growth of 9.3 per cent in the corresponding 
period of 2007-08. 
 The RBI in their Mid-Term Review of Annual Policy for the year 2008-09 have maintained 
their projection made during the Annual Policy Review in April 2008, for inflation at 7 percent by 
end March 2009, keeping in view the supply ma nagement measures taken by the Government 
and the lagged demand response to the monetary policy measures taken by the RBI over the 
last one year. RBI’s endeavour is to bring down inflation to a tolerable level of below 5 per cent at 
the earliest, while aiming for convergence with the global average inflation of around 3.0 per cent 
over the medium term. 
 (c) and (d) Though growth rate of between 7 to 8 per cent represents some slow down 
from the high average growth of around 8.8 per cent in the last five years, this should be seen in 
the context that in the previous six-years (1997-98 to 2002-03) there was not even one year in 
which growth exceeded 7 per cent. 
 The growth in the first half of 2008-09 is ch aracterized by an increase in the ratio of 
Government Consumption Expenditure component in the demand side of GDP, emanating from 
enhanced public expenditure directed towards promoting improved access to essential services, 
infrastructure development and rural prosperity aimed towards inclusive growth which impact the 
common man.

due to the deepening global financial crisis;

 (c) the details of action taken for la bour intensive projects, if any; and 
 (d) the expected loss of employment in the country due to the deepening global financial 
crisis for the period 2008-10, year-wise and category-wise? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINI STRY OF FINANCE (SHRI PAWAN KUMAR 
BANSAL): (a) to (d) Unlike the developed countr ies where job losses have been reported due 
to the global financial crisis, the impact has b een limited in India as a large proportion of 
population is employed in the ag riculture sector which has been relatively not affected by the 
crisis. Besides, the services sector with a large share in GDP has also been less affected. Even 
in the export sector which registered negative growth in October, 2008, the fall was mainly due 
to a spike in export growth in October, 2007 and is limited to some sectors only. While no

Impact of global economic recession 
 †*320. SHRI PRABHAT JHA: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
 (a) whether it is a fact that India is also affected by global economic recession; 
 (b) if so, the details thereof; 
 (c) whether Government has formulated any scheme or set up any Commission to assess 
the effects of this economic recession; 
 (d) if so, the effects of the recessi on on different sectors so far; and 
 (e) if not, the manner in which Government would assess the fallout of this recession? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINI STRY OF FINANCE (SHRI PAWAN KUMAR 
BANSAL): (a) and (b) The Glob al economic recession has impacted the domestic economy. 
As per the estimates released by the Central Statis tical Organisation of Ministry of Statistics and 
Programme Implementation, the growth rate of  the economy, measured in terms of Gross 
Domestic Product at factor cost, was 7.8 per cent in the first half (April-September) of the 
financial year 2008-09 as against the growth of 9.3 percent in the first half of 2007-08. 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 

 32
 The growth in the first half of 2008-09 for agri culture, industry and services are estimated at 
2.9 per cent, 6.5 per cent and 9.8 per cent as compared to 4.5 per cent. 9.3 per cent and 10.7 
per cent in the corresponding period of 2007-08. There are signs of slowdown in growth across 
different sectors. 
 The global slowdown has its implications on the domestic economy, primarily through the 
moderation in capital flows, the financial markets and trade. The impact of the global crisis on 
the domestic economy has been largely transmitte d directly through the Indian equity and the 
foreign exchange markets and through trade channels and indirectly through the money, debt 
and credit markets. While exact effects of the global slowdown are difficult to quantify 
because the complexity of the crisis and spreading effects in the international economy, it is 
expected that there may be some moderation in India’s capital flows and in the growth of 
exports. 
 (c) to (e) The Government has not set up any Commission to assess the impact of the 
global economic recession. The Government monitors  and evaluates, from time to time, at the 
highest official and political levels the effect of global economic develo pments on the Indian 
economy in formulating its economic policies and designs counter cyclical steps accordingly. To 
safeguard the economy against adverse impact of the global financial crisis, the Reserve Bank of 
India has taken measures, ‘Inter alia’, for reduction in Cash Reserve Ratio and Statutory Liquidity 
Ratio, reduction in repo and reverse repo rates and for liberalising access to external commercial 
borrowings. The Government has announced a fi scal package which includes additional plan 
expenditure, reduction in the ‘ad valorem’ Cenvat rate and measures to support exports. These 
measures have ensured the effective functionin g of the financial system and improvement in 
liquidity in the money market and provide stimulus to the economy to counter the slowdown in 
growth.

PATEL): (a) and (b) No foreign registered aircraft is allowed to operate to/from and within 
India in an unrestricted manner, except as a pa rt of approved internat ional itinerary. Prior 
approval of Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) is required to operate foreign

 (i) High antiquity of its early texts/recorded history over a period of 1500-2000 years.

 (iii) The literacy tradition be original and not borrowed from another speech community.

discontinuity between the classical language and its later forms or its offshoots.

 2365. SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
 (a) whether the futures trading policy of Gove rnment has resulted in extreme inflation and 
has encouraged the practice of speculation to a greater extent; 
 (b) whether it is a fact that billions of Indian  currency is going abroad leading to hike in 
most of the commodities as a result thereof; 
 (c) whether Government would consider imposing ban on futures, trading in order to 
check inflation; 
 (d) if so, by when; and 
 (e) if not, the reasons therefor? 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 

 66
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINI STRY OF FINANCE (SHRI PAWAN KUMAR 
BANSAL): (a) The Expert Committee chaired by Professor Abhijit Sen, Member, Planning 
Commission, constituted by the Government in  March, 2007 to study the impact of futures 
trading on the prices of agricult ural commodities has stated that in view of conflicting results 
from daily, as against weekly and monthly data, no strong conclusion can be drawn on whether 
introduction of futures trade is associated with d ecrease or increase in spot price volatility. The 
Expert Committee also analyzed an nual growth rate in prices of sensitive commodities (food 
grains and sugar) in pre-future period and post future period and concluded that although 
inflation clearly increased post-futures in some se nsitive commodities that have higher weight in 
consumer price indices, it is not possible to ma ke any general claim that inflation accelerated 
more in commodities with futures trading. As on December 6, 2008, the inflation rate measured 
by the Wholesale Price Index stood at 6.84 percent, compared to 12.91 percent on  
August 2, 2008. 
 (b) Futures trading in commodities in India does  not appear to lead to any flight of Indian 
currency abroad. 
 (c) to (e) As a matter of caution, the Fo rward Markets Commission (FMC) had suspended 
futures trading in tur, urad, wheat and rice in 2007. Subsequently, the FMC had suspended 
futures trading in chana, soy oil, potato and rubber w.e.f. 7.05.08, which was not extended 
beyond 30.11.08. Since the Abhijit Sen Committee could not establish any definite causal 
relationship between futures tradin g and rice in prices of commodities there is no proposal to 
ban futures trading in more commodities.

 2369. SHRI PRAKASH JAVADEKAR: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
 (a) whether it is a fact that more than 60 million farmers out of total farming community of 
India have not received any benefit of loan waiver scheme declared by Government;

farmers who have not been benefited in the present scheme? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINI STRY OF FINANCE (SHRI PAWAN KUMAR 
BANSAL): (a) and (b) Government of India has implemented Agricultural Debt Waiver and Debt 
Relief (ADWDR) Scheme, 2008, which covered all direct agricultural loans extended to ‘marginal 
and small farmers’ and ‘other farmers’  by Scheduled Commercial Banks, Regional Rural Banks, 
Cooperative Credit Institutions (including Urban Cooperative Banks) and Local Area Banks that 
were disbursed during the period from April 1, 1997 to March 31, 2007, were overdue on

crore ‘other farmers’ have benefitted from the Sc heme involving debt waiver and debt relief of 
Rs. 65,318.33 crore. 
 (c) The prime objective of the ADWDR Scheme was to cover all those farmers who, for 
some reason or the other, could not pay back th eir overdues to the banks and therefore, were 
under continued indebtedness. Such farmers, as a result, could not borrow from the banking 
system. ADWDR Scheme was designed to de-clog this line of credit and help such needy 
farmers, making them eligible for fresh credit in the process.

more Grievance Redressal Officers (GROs) for ea ch State (having regard to the number of 
branches in that State). The name and address of the GRO concerned have been displayed in 
each branch of the lending institution. The GRO has the authority to receive representations from 
aggrieved farmers and pass appropriate orders thereon.

 (a) whether the World Bank has in its report on “Global Financial Crisis ” has pointed out 
that India has taken measures to tide over global financial crisis;

 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINI STRY OF FINANCE (SHRI PAWAN KUMAR 
BANSAL): (a) Yes, Madam. The World Bank, in its analysis titled “Global Financial Crisis: 
Implications for South Asia ” dated October 21, 2008 has mentioned about measures taken by 
India to tide over global financial crisis. 
 (b) and (c) Yes, Madam. The World Bank has agreed to provide an additional assistance

Initiatives to improve tax revenues and disposal of refund claims 
 2372. SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN PANY: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
 (a) whether it is a fact that Government ha s taken new initiatives to improve tax revenues 
and also to expedite disposal of refund claims; 
 (b) if so, the details thereof;

number of refund claims have been piled up  and there is no mechanism to address the

 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI S.S. 
PALANIMANICKAM): (a) Yes, Sir. The Government has taken some new initiatives to improve 
the tax revenues and also to expedite the disposal of refund claims. 

 75
 (b) The following steps have been taken by  the Government to improve the direct and 
indirect tax revenues: 
 (I) Direct Taxes  
  1. Monitoring of advance tax payment of top tax payers. 
  2. Emphasis on collection out of arrear demand and monitoring of the cases of top 
defaulters. 
  3. Selection of cases under scrutiny based on objective financial parameters.  
  4. Computerization of the Departmental business processes and data bases for 
linking of information and reporting of high value transactions. 
  5. Strengthening the tax deduction at sources/Tax Collection at sources set up by 
creating 13 Commissioner level posts and conducting effective surveys to unearth 
non-payment of TDS/TCS. 
  6. Encouragement to voluntary tax-comp liance through better taxpayer’s service. 
  7. Multi-media campaign to encour age voluntary compliance of tax laws.  
  8. Increase in efforts for widening of the tax base. 
  9. Generating lists of cases in which self assessment tax was not paid and pursuing 
recovery. 
  Steps taken by the Government to expe dite the disposal of refund claims:- 
  (i) Guidelines have been issued by Cent ral Board of Direct Taxes to process all  
returns within four months of filing and issue refunds. 
  (ii) To ensure speedy processing and issuance of refunds for the assessment year 
2007-08, the Income Tax Department has instructed the field formations to accept 
the tax-payer’s claim for the credit of th e Tax Deduction at Source (TDS) at the 
time of processing of returns in all th e IT returns where th e aggregate TDS claim 
does not exceed Rs. 5 lakhs and where the refund computed does not exceed 
Rs. 25,000. 
 (II) Indirect Tax 
 I. Measures to tackle evasion in central excise: 
  (i) Information from Third party:  In order to identify manufac turers with a  propensity 
to evade taxes and to create an atmosphere of voluntary compliance, certain legal 
changes were made in September, 2008 in the Central Excise Rules to facilitate 
collection of information from third party sources or from manufacturers 
themselves. These measures in clude- (a) prescribing an Annual Installed 
Capacity Return for giving the annual production capacity of the plant. The annual 
capacity as declared by a manufacturer  would be compared with the actual 
production declared by a unit and in ca se off significant variations, necessary 
enquiries would be made; (b) collecting additional information such as PAN, VAT 

 76
Registration No. and Electricity Meter details from SSI Units; (c) collecting 
Electricity Consumption Data; (d) Filing of ER-4, ER-5 and ER-6 returns by more 
assessees. 
  (ii) Deterrent provisions: Deterrent provisions were introduced for Central Excise in 
December, 2006 to deal firmly with the problem of planned and deliberate non-
compliance of tax law. Where a manufacturer is prima facie found to be knowingly 
involved in committing specified offences , then the facility of monthly payment of 
duty and/or utilisation of CENVAT credit  can be withdrawn/restricted. If the 
manufacturer is found to be involved in committing any of the specified offences 
for the second time or subsequently, then  physical control can be imposed for a 
period of time. 
 II. Large Taxpayer Units: Following international practice, large tax payer units are being 
set up in Indian in a phased manner. An LTU is a self-contained tax office under the 
Department of Revenue acting as a single window clearance point for all matters 
relating to Central Excise, Income Tax/Corporate Tax and Service Tax. Eligible Tax 
Payers (who have paid duties of excise of service tax of more than rupees five crores in 
cash; or advance tax of more than rupees ten crores, under the Income Tax Act, 1961) 
and opt for assessment in LTU shall be able to file their excise return, direct taxes 
returns and service tax return at such LTUs and will be assessed to all these taxes. 
 III. CAAP Audit: The Department has extended the Computer Assisted Audit Protocol 
(CAAP) to 4 new centres, in addition to the existing 5 centres. CAAP is a method of 
audit for scrutiny of financial data of assesses with the help of specialized software 
installed in the CAAP Lab in the offi ce of the respective Central Excise 
commissionerate. With its help, the linkages and discrepancies in the assessees’ data 
can be detected and the areas of non-compliance can be identified. 
 IV. Refunds: For expeditious disposal of refund claims, instructions were issued for 
sanctioning of 80% of refund claim within 15 days of filing of the claim after completing 
preliminary scrutiny to specified category of manufacturers/exporters. The balance 
amount is to be paid within 45 days from th e date of filing of the claim. Further, as per 
the provisions of the Central Excise Act, 1944 if the refund claim is not sanctioned 
within three months from the filling of the clai m, the department is liable to pay interest 
at the prescribed rate to the applicant.

Fall in foreign exchange reserves 
 2375. SHRI DARA SINGH: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
 (a) whether the country’s Central Bank has seen its foreign exchange reserves  
shrink more than 63 billion dollars in less than six months as well as our exports slumping; 
 (b) whether it is a fact that the country’s  forex reserves which touched as high as 316 
billion dollars on May 23 started falling at an alarming pace and on October, 31 stood at 253 
billion dollars; 
 (c) if so, the reasons therefor; and 
 (d) what remedial steps Government has ta ken so far to minimize the draw down on 
reserves indicating what efforts are under way to revive exports growth also? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINI STRY OF FINANCE (SHRI PAWAN KUMAR 
BANSAL): (a) to (c) The foreig n exchange reserves (including  gold, Special Drawing Rights 
and Reserve Tranche Position in the I.M.F. wa s placed at US $ 316.2 billion on May 23, 2008. 
With the deepening of the global financial crisis  in September 2008, there has been a withdrawal 
of US dollar investments/funds from global markets, including India to some extent resulting in 
the appreciation of US dollar against major world currencies. The exchange rate of the rupee vis-
á-vis US dollar had depreciated sharply in October, 2008 breaching the Rs. 50 Mark. While 
exports grew robustly at 29.5 per cent during–April-August 2008, there was deceleration in 
October, 2008 (10.4 per cent) and a decline in October, 2008 (-12.1 per cent) on account of a 
spike in export growth in October, 2007. However, growth in exports for April-October, 2008 is 
at 23.7 per cent over the level in April-October, 2007. This also contributed to the tight supply 
conditions in the foreign exchange market. For maintaining orderly conditions and to augment 
foreign currency liquidity in the foreign exchange  market. For maintaining orderly conditions and 
to augment foreign currency liquidity in the fore ign exchange market, the Reserve Bank of India 
(RBI) intervened through sale of US dollars. Thus due to the cumulative effect of the sale of US 
dollars by RBI and the valuation loss arising fr om the appreciation of US dollars, the foreign 
exchange  reserves declined to a level of US $ 252.9 billion on October 31, 2008 and further to a 
level of US $ 245.9 billion on December 5, 2008. 

 79
 (d) The level of foreign exchange reserves is largely the outcome of the Reserve Bank’s 
intervention in the foreign exchange market to  smoothen exchange rate volatility and valuation 
changes due to movement of US dollar against other major currencies of the world. Foreign 
exchange reserves are accumulated when there is an absorption of the excess foreign exchange 
flows by the RBI through interven tion in the foreign market and vice versa. The present level of 
foreign exchange reserves is adequate to meet emerging balance of payments situation in the 
short to medium term. A slew of measures have been taken to improve foreign exchange inflows 
and boost exports. Which inter ala include: 
 1. The interest rate ceilings on FCNR (B) and NR(E) RA term deposits were raised to 
LIBOR / Swap rates plus 100 basis points and 175 basis points respectively, so as to 
attract more foreign currency deposits from NRIs. 
 2. External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs) up to US $ 500 million per borrower per 
financial year were permitted for rupee expenditure and/or foreign currency 
expenditure for permissible end uses under the automatic route. 
 3. The all-in-cost ceiling for ECBs for average maturity period of 3 years and up to 5 years 
has been enhanced to 300 basis points above LIBOR and to 500 basis points above 
LIBOR for ECBs over 5 years. 
 4. The all-in-cost ceiling for trade credit of less than 3 years was enhanced to 6 months 
LIBOR plus 200 basis points. 
 5. Pre and post shipment export cr edit for labour intensive exports, i.e., textiles 
(including handlooms, carpets and handicra fts), leather, gems and jewellery, marine 
products and SME sector is being made mo re attractive by providing an interest 
subvention of 2 percent upto 31/3/2009 subject to minimum rate of interest of 7 
percent per annum.

 Subsequently, on the invitation  of the United States of America (USA), the G-20 Summit on

proposed to carry forward the commitments in the Summit Declaration by constituting few G20

the company. This perception is influenced by many factors including the macro-economic 
environment, the growth potential of the ec onomy, policy credibility of the government, 
corporate performance, domestic and international events and market sentiments. 
 The Exchanges and the regulators do not try to manage or control market movements. 
Their endeavour is to build systems and practi ces and deepen and broaden markets which can 
withstand volatility. They have put in place systems and practices to promote a safe, transparent 
and efficient market and to protect market integrity. The systems instituted include advanced risk 
management mechanisms comprising on-line monitoring and surveillance, various limits on 
positions, margin requirements, circuit filters,  etc. Measures taken to broaden and deepen 
markets include: screen based trading system, de materialization of securities, corporatization 
and demutualization of exchanges, settlement through clearing corporation, trading in 
derivatives, etc.

Services and Products Ltd., (IISL), a joint venture between National Stock Exchange and

 As per the conditions of licensing, SGX has the right to list and offer for trading, futures and 
options contracts based on S and P CNX NIFTY on a non-exclusive basis.

of restrictions on issuance of  Overseas Derivate Instruments in October, 2008, permission for

covers index future positions also.

Effects of global recession 
 †2407. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER SINGH MAJITHA: 
  SHRI RAM JETHMALANI: 
 Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
 (a) whether it is a fact that several st eps have been taken between August, 2008 and 
December, 2008 to neutralise the effects of recession in India brought on by global melt down; 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 

 106
 (b) if so, the details of these steps an d when they were taken in the country; 
 (c) the total additional amount each of the measure brought to economy in its wake; and 
 (d) the extent of decline estimated to be brought in economy due to recession? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINI STRY OF FINANCE (SHRI PAWAN KUMAR 
BANSAL): (a) to (c) The Indian economy is not in recession . There has been a moderation in 
the growth of the domestic economy due to the impact of the global meltdown. The Government 
and the Reserve Bank of India have taken variou s contra cyclical measures to safeguard the 
economy against adverse impact of the global  financial crisis. These measures since mid 
September, Inter alia  include reduction in Cash Reserve Ratio and Statutory Liquidity Ratio, 
reduction in repo and reverse repo rates, libera lising access to external commercial borrowings, 
a fiscal package which includes additional plan expenditures, reduction in the ad valorem Cenvat 
rate and measures to support exports. 
 (d) The combined impact of these measures is expected to have counter cyclical Impact 
on the domestic growth moderation. Quantify ing and apportioning the gains between each 
measure is not feasible. As per RBI the GDP growth forecast for 2008-09 ranges between 7.5-
8.0 percent. The real GDP growth during 2007-08 as per the Central Statistical Organisation is 
placed at 9 per cent.

Foreign exchange reserves 
 2412. SHRI RAMA CHANDRA KHUNTIA: Will th e PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
 (a) whether it is a fact the foreign exchange reserves of India has been reduced to a great 
extent and the value of Indian rupee also has been considerably reduced as compared to the US 
dollar; 
 (b) if so, whether it will have a negative impact on our economy; and 
 (c) if so, the details thereof? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINI STRY OF FINANCE (SHRI PAWAN KUMAR 
BANSAL): (a) to (c) The exchange rate of the rupee moved from a level of Rs.39.97/US $  
as on  end-March  2008 to Rs.44.21/US $ on  September 1, 2008 and further to a peak of 

 111 
Rs.50.52/US $ on December 2, 2008. US dollar gaining strength against major world 
currencies, outflows on account of Foreign Instit utional Investment, reduced net capital inflows 
and widening trade deficit arising from elevated levels of global oil and commodity prices in the 
first half of the financial year are some of the fa ctors that could be attributed for the depreciation 
of the rupee. For maintaining orderly conditions and to augment foreign currency liquidity in the 
foreign exchange market, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intervened through sale of US dollars. 
Due to the cumulative effect of the sale of US dollars by RBI and the valuation loss arising from 
the appreciation of US dollars against major wo rld currencies, the foreign exchange reserves 
declined to a level of US $ 245.9 billion on December 5, 2008. The present level of foreign 
exchange reserves is adequate to meet emerging  balance of payments situation in the short to 
medium term. The real macroeconomic impact  of a global slowdown will differ between 
economies in which net exports are a major driver of growth and those like India in which foreign 
net demand plays a relatively lower role. The macroeconomic impact of the global financial 
turmoil on India has been relatively smaller due to the overall strength of domestic demand, the 
predominantly domestic nature of financing of investment and the structure of the economy; 
nevertheless with greater openness of the Indian economy relative to earlier periods, some slow 
down is likely in the short-run.

Diesel) and Import Parity (for Kerosene and LPG) to Free on Board (FOB) Export 
Parity basis). 
 (ii) The price of Petrol be adjusted to fully  reflect international prices by March, 2009 and 
the price of Diesel be adjusted to fully reflect international prices in 24 months time. 
 (iii) Sale of Diesel to industrial and commerc ial users be at market prices to be negotiated 
on commercial considerations. 
 (iv) Once these price adjustments are comple ted, Government should disengage from the 
process of pricing of petroleum products, and allow pricing to be an outcome of a 
competitive market process. 
 (v) Subsidies on LPG (Domestic) and SKO (P DS) should be restricted to BPL families 
only. This subsidy should be delivered through Smart Cards or cash transfer in  
urban and semi-urban areas and not through supply of products below their market 
prices. 
 (vi) For Domestic LPG, the entitlement to subsidised supply should be reduced to 6 refills 
in a year, which could be progressively reduced to 4 refills, 2 refills and zero refills  in 
the following years. 
 The recommendations made by the Committee are under consideration of the Government.

 †2466. SHRI AJAY SINGH CHAUTALA: Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state:

 (a) whether it is a fact that incidents of at tack on foreign tourists and women in various

women tourists?

‘Police’ are State subjects as per the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India. As such, the 
prevention of crime, including crimes against to urists and women is the primary responsibility of 
State Governments/Union Territories. However, in order to ensure safety and security of 
tourists, the Ministry of Tourism has advise d all the State Governments/Union Territory

Kashmir, Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, Punjab, Madhya Pradesh and Orissa have deployed Tourist 
Police in one form or the other. 
 Ministry of Tourism in consultation with Ministry of Home Affairs, Ministry of Defence and 
State Governments/Union Territory Administrations, has framed guidelines for formation of 
Tourist Security Organization(s ) comprising Ex–Servicemen, fo r the safety and security of 
tourists. The guidelines have been sent to State Government and Union Territory 
Administrations.

Leakage of dams 
 2474. SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN: Will the Minister of WATER RESOURCES be pleased to 
state: 
 (a) whether there are reports on leakage of water from various dams for the last three 
years; 
 (b) if so, the details including the life period of such dams fixed during the construction 
period, State-wise, category-wise and year-wise for the last three years; 
 (c) if so, the steps taken to rectify the ab ove leak in details, State-wise and category-
wise; 
 (d) if so, whether steps will be taken to construct new dams to replace above old dams; 
and 
 (e) if not, the reasons therefor? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINI STRY OF WATER RESOURCES (SHRI JAY 
PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) to (c) Seepage for the dams upto a permissible limit is a 
normal phenomenon. The project authorities collect information about leakage/seepage of water 
from most of the dams and take remedial measures  in case of seepage in excess of permissible 
limits. As BIS 12182 the feasible service time of i rrigation and hydropower projects shall not be 
less than 100 and 70 years respectively. 
 The State Governments are mainly the owners of irrigation and mult ipurpose projects. As 
such the responsibility of maintenance of the dams  and their safety rests with them. The role of 
Central Government is confined to giving advisory  services and framing guidelines with regard to 
safety and rehabilitation of dams. 

 157
 (d) and (e) A decision to re place an old dam with a new dam cannot be taken only on the 
basis of seepage through the dam. Such a situatio n may arise only if all avenues to restore the 
safety of the dam as well as functional capabilit y of the dam have been exhausted. All possible 
alternatives need to be examined by the Stat e Governments/owners of the dam from techno-
economic considerations. 
Alarming level of ground water in Delhi 
 2475. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN: Will the Minister of WATER RESOURCES be pleased to 
state: 
 (a) whether Government is aware that groundwater levels in various parts of the country 
particularly in Delhi have dipped alarmingly low; 
 (b) if so, whether the Central Ground- Wa ter Authority (CGWA) have conducted any 
survey to know the factors responsible for dipping of groundwater levels; 
 (c) if so, the details thereof; and 
 (d) the steps taken by Government to  ensure proper groundwater levels?. 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINI STRY OF WATER RESOURCES (SHRI JAY 
PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) to (d) As per studies conducted by the Central Ground 
Water Board (CGWB), decline in the level of gr ound water has been observed in various  
parts of the country including NCT Delhi due to withdrawal of ground water in excess of annual 
recharge. 
 Government has taken following steps to ensure proper ground water levels:- 
  Implementation of a scheme on Artific ial Recharge to ground water through Dug 
wells. 
  Implementation of a demonstrative scheme on Rain Water Harves ting and Artificial 
R e c h a r g e  t o  G r o u n d  W a t e r   i n  i d e ntified areas duri ng the period  
2006-09. 
  Circulation of Model Bill to States/UTs to facilitate ground water regulation and water 
harvesting for artificial recharge. 
  Organization of National Ground Water Cong ress for sharing information and achieving 
coordination among stakeholders. 
  Constitution of Advisory Council on Artific ial Recharge of Ground Water to popularize 
the concept of artificial recharge among stakeholders. 
  Setting up of Central Ground Water Author ity (CGWA) for the pu rpose of Regulation 
and Control of Ground Water Management and Development. 
Development of Water Management 
 2476. SHRIMATI MOHSINA KIDWAI: Will the Minister of WATER RESOURCES be pleased 
to state: 

 158
 (a) whether several State Governments have ur ged the Central Government to further relax 
the guidelines for inclusion of schemes and a ssistance under Accelerated Irrigation Benefit 
Programme, Repair, Renovation and Restoration of water bodies and Command Areas 
Development and Water Management; 
 (b) if so, the reaction of the Central Government thereto; 
 (c) whether the grants to various States for irrigation schemes are provided as per the 
recommendations of the Thirteenth Finance Commission; and 
 (d) if so, the details thereof? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINI STRY OF WATER RESOURCES (SHRI JAY 
PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) and (b) Requests from the State Governments for 
modifications/further liberalization of guidelines of the Programme  and examination/modification 
in the guidelines is a continuous process taken up by the Ministry of Water Resources from time 
to time. Guidelines for Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme were last amended in 
December 2006 by the Central Government making them more liberal and oriented to giving 
major thrust to development of irrigation facilitie s in drought prone/tribal areas, in the States 
having irrigation development below national average and in agrarian distressed districts of 
Andhra Pradesh. Karnataka, Ke rala and Maharashtra included in the Prime Minister’s relief 
package. For the Command Area Developmen t and Water Management programme, the 
condition of inclusion of project only against co mpletion/deletion of a project has been relaxed 
for the remaining four years of Eleventh Plan (2008-09 to 2011-12) for projects in the Prime 
Ministers package for agra rian distressed districts, projec ts in drought prone/tribal areas, 
projects in States having irrigation development below national average an d projects in special 
category States/areas i.e., North Eastern Region, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Jammu and 
Kashmir and Kalahandi Bolangir Koraput (KBK) districts of Orissa. 
 (c) and (d) The grants to the State Governme nts are provided as per guidelines of these 
programmes approved by the Central Government.

 2477. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will the Mini ster of WATER RESOURCES be pleased to 
state: 
 (a) whether the State-run Jammu and Kashmir Power Development Corporation has 
affected the changes in the design of Baglihar power project as suggested by the neutral expert 
of the World Bank of adjudicate the dispute between India and Pakistan; 
 (b) whether Pakistan has expr essed its satisfaction over India’s willingness to affect 
changes as suggested by the World Bank expert; and 
 (c) if so, the details thereof? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINI STRY OF WATER RESOURCES (SHRI JAY 
PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) Yes, Sir. Jammu and Kashmir State Power Development 
Corporation (JKSPDC) has carried out the change s in the design of Bagliahar Hydroelectric 

 159
Plant as suggested by the Neutral Expert appointed by the World Bank on Pakistan’s request, 
for Expert Determination on the points of difference raised by Pakistan. 
 (b) During a Tour of Inspection of Perm anent Indus Commission to the Baglihar 
Hydroelectric Project held on 30th July 2008 on Pakistan’s request, the changes suggested by 
the Neutral Expert and implemented by JKSPDC, were verified by Pakistan. 
 (c) The Neutral Expert had suggested that the power intake level of Baglihar Hydroelectric 
Plant should be raised by 3.0 m and the top level of dam should be reduced by 1.5 m. Under the 
provision of Treaty, the decision of the Neutral Ex pert on the matter is final and binding upon the

 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINI STRY OF WATER RESOURCES (SHRI JAY

Circumstances leading to the death of Shri Hemant Karkare and other 
officers of the Mumbai Police 
 THE MINISTER OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM): Sir, recently, some 
questions have been raised about the circumstances  in which three police officers including Shri 
Hemant Karkare, head of the ATS, Mumbai, were killed while travelling in one car on Rang 
Bhawan Lane, near Cama Hospital on November 26, 2008. I have ascertained the facts from the 
Government of Maharashtra. 
 At the outset, I wish to say that there are at least three eye witnesses to the incident, one of 
them being Mohammed Ajmal Amir who was appreh ended shortly after the incident and is now 
in the custody of the police. The other two eye witnesses are Shri Arun Jadhav, a police Naik 
who was in the Qualis vehicle when the incident occurred, and Shri Maruti Madhavrao Phad, the 
driver of a Government vehicle provided for the use of the Principal Secretary (Health), 
Government of Maharashtra. 
 Based on the accounts given by these three eye witnesses and the accounts of other 
witnesses, the Mumbai Police have been able to reconstruct the sequence of events. Briefly, the 
following is the sequence:- 
 Shri Karkare reached his residence at Dadar at about 21:45 hrs. Shortly thereafter, on 
receiving information over teleph one from Shri Tondwalkar, Insp ector-in-charge of the Control 
Room, he alerted his staff to be prepared to rush to the CST Railway Station. Within minutes, he 
and his team (one PSI and four Constables) took  a Bolero jeep and rushed towards the CST. 
Before they reached the CST, they found that the road had been blocked due to a nakabandi. 
Hence, Shri Karkare and his team walked from that point to the CST. He was met by Shri K.P. 
Raghuvanshi, Additional DGP, Railways, and other officers. They informed Shri Karkare that two 
terrorists, after opening indiscriminate fire insi de the Railway Station, had fled towards a lane 
(called Anjuman Lane) between the Times of India building and Anjuman Islam High School. 
Immediately, Shri Karkare put on his bullet pr oof jacket and helmet and along with his team 

 204
rushed in the direction in which the terrorists had fled. Shri Karkare an d his team reached the 
rear gate of Cama Hospital. They heard the no ise of exchange of fire as well as blast of 
grenades. They took cover position behind the rear gate. 
 Shortly thereafter, Shri Asho k Kamte, Additional CP, Mumbai, reached the rear gate of 
Cama Hospital. Earlier, Shri Kamte had reached his residence at about 22.00 hrs. Within five 
minutes, on receiving information from the Contro l Room of the East Region, he instructed his 
wireless operator and driver to get ready to leave and he left within the next ten minutes. He took 
the road inside the Bombay Port Trust. When he  reached Azad Maidan Police club, he was told 
that he could not take the car to the rear gate of Cama Hospital. Hence, he got down from his 
car, directed his driver to wait in the car and, along with his wireless operator, walked to the rear 
gate of Cama Hospital. 
 Shri Vijay Salaskar, Police Inspector, Anti Extortion Squad, Crime Branch, also reached the 
rear gate of Cama Hospital. Earlier, he had reached home at about 21:30 hrs and relieved his 
driver, staff and car. However, at about 21:50 hrs, on receiving information on his mobile from 
the Additional Commissio ner, Crime Branch, he left his residence driving his private Qualis 
vehicle. En route, after alerting Shri Arun Jadhav, his Police Naik, over telephone, he fetched 
Shri Nitin Alaknure, Police Inspector, and both drove towards Colaba Police Station via Haji Ali 
and Napean Sea Road. At Colaba Police Station, Arun Jadhav, the Police Naik, joined him. Shri 
Salaskar was instructed through mobile phone by Shri Rakesh Maria, Joint CP (Crime) to rush 
to Mumbai Police Headquarters. While driving to the Headquarters, Shri Salaskar spotted two 
armed policemen standing alert at  the gate of Azad Maidan Police Station. They informed Shri 
Salaskar about the shootout near Cama Hospital. Hence, Shri Salaskar ru shed to the rear gate 
of Cama Hospital with his team.  
 From the facts narrated above, it would be se en that the three officers, Shri Karkare, Shri 
Kamte and Shri Salaskar, converged at the rear  gate of Cama Hospital through independent 
routes. While the three were discussing the si tuation amongst themselves, Shri Telekar, the 
wireless operator attached to Shri Sadanand Date, Additional CP, came out of the Cama 
Hospital with injuries and informed them that Shri Sadanand Date had been injured in an 
exchange of gunfire with the terrorists inside the Cama Hospital premises. There was some firing 
from the terrace of the Cama Hospital, but suddenly, there was silence. This was followed by the 
sound of firing from the direction of St. Xavier’s  College. Shri Karkare directed his team to take 
position at the same spot and, accompanied by  Shri Kamte and Shri Salaskar, got into the 
police jeep, a Qualis vehicle, belonging to the ACP, Pydhonie Division, and drove in the direction 
of St. Xavier’s College. Shri Salaskar was at the wheel, Shri Kamte sat on the left side of the 
front seat, Shri Karkare was in the middle seat, an d four others, including Shri Arun Jadhav, sat 
on the rear seat. 
 Shri Arun Jadhav, the surviving policeman, ha s stated that the Qualis was passing the ATM 
Centre of a Bank located on Rang Bhawan Lane, off Badruddin Tayyabji Marg, when two 
terrorists opened indiscriminate fire from behind the bushes on the other side of the lane. One of 

 205
the occupants of the Qualis vehicle returned the fi re which caused injuries to the hand of one of 
the terrorists (later identified as Mohammed Aj mal Amir). Shri Karkare, Shri Kamte, Shri 
Salaskar and three others were gravely injured.  The two terrorists pulled out the three injured 
officers from the front and middle seats and hijack ed the Qualis vehicle along with the four men 
whom the terrorists believed were dead. Shri Arun Jadhav was covered by the bodies of his 
three colleagues, who were killed, and thus remained undetected. The Qualis vehicle was 
abandoned at Free Press Journal Marg and the two terrorists hijacked a Skoda car. At this point, 
Shri Arun Jadhav got out of the vehicle and repo rted the incident to the control room using the 
wireless set in the Qualis vehicle. The control room received the report at 00:25 hrs, that is 
shortly after midnight of 26th/27th November, 2008. 
 Shri Arun Jadhav has accoun ted for the events between the time when he joined Shri 
Salaskar at Colaba Police Station and the time he made the report to the control room. The 
apprehended terrorist, Mohammed Ajmal Amir, has corroborated the portion of the story where 
he and his companion opened fire on a Qualis ve hicle, believed that all the occupants had been 
killed, and hijacked the vehicle. Shri Maruti Madhavrao Phad, driver of the official vehicle 
provided to the Principal Secretary (Health), Government of Maharashtra, had witnessed the 
incident from a close distance. He is a witness to the movements of the two terrorists who took 
cover behind some bushes and fired on the Qualis vehicle, pulled out three injured men and 
eventually hijacked the vehicle. 
 The Crime Branch of Mumbai Police is invest igating the offences, including the offences 
suspected to be committed by Mohammed Ajmal Amir and his companion, since identified as 
Ismail Khan. The investigators have reconstructed the sequence of events by talking to a number 
of people including police officers and policemen who were present at different locations. The 
investigators have reached the conclusion that Shri Karkare took the most convenient route from 
his residence at Dadar (East) to the CST Railway  Station and, after conferring with the police 
officers at the Railway Station, decided to proceed to Cama Hospital. It is at the rear gate of 
Cama Hospital that he was joined by Shri Kamte and Shri Salaskar. The sequence of events after 
the three officers and four men boarded the Qualis vehicle at the rear gate of Cama Hospital and 
until they were fired upon near the ATM Centre of a Bank on Rang Bhawan Lane have been 
reconstructed on the basis of the eye witness ac counts of Shri Arun Jadhav and Shri Maruti 
Madhavrao Phad. 
 The investigators have reached the conclusion  that there is no truth whatsoever in the 
suspicion that there was a conspiracy to eliminate Shri Karkare or others. There is also no truth 
in the different versions that have been circulated about the movement of Shri Karkare on that 
fateful day. Shri Karkare appears to have acted, after conferring with his colleagues, with speed 

 206
and purpose in response to a crisis situation. While it is, indeed, unfo rtunate that three brave 
officers and their men boarded one Qualis vehicle, the circumstances in which they came under 
fire and were killed were tragically fortuitous. 
 In the days before his death, questions were raised about the genuineness of the 
investigations that were being conducted by Shri  Karkare in a terrorist case. After his death, 
questions are being raised about the circumstances in which he was killed. In my view, both are 
wrong and deeply regrettable. 
 Mr. Deputy Chairman, Sir, I wish to end this statement with an appeal to all hon. Members 
and my fellow citizens. This is the time to salute  the dedication and bravery of the police officers 
and their men. This is the time to help their fam ilies, especially their children, to cope with the 
tragedy. This is the time for th e whole country to stand united and carry on a determined fight 
against terror.

 MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, the 214th Se ssion of Rajya Sabha comes to a close. I 
have directed the Secretary-General to make av ailable statistical information regarding this 
Session. This has been a difficult year. The nation has faced unprecedented and heinous 
terrorist attacks. We also faced serious economic crisis, globally and nationally. 2008 would also 
go down in our Parliamentary history as the year when the House had its lowest number of 
annual sittings — a mere 46 sitti ngs for the calendar year. Yet, I am also grateful for the 
immense cooperation that I have received from ho n. Members that has enabled the introduction 
of new initiatives for the smooth conduct of Hous e proceedings, specially the three-minute rule 
for the Zero Hour. 
 Hon. Members the raison d’etre of our ex istence is enacting legislation after due 
deliberation and ensuring the accountability of the Executive. While much legislative activity has 
taken place in this Session, the passing of important legislative business in the din does no credit 
to our Parliament. Apart from its inherent undesirability, the absence of parliamentary debate 
would not help future generations in ascertaining the legislative intent. The contrast with the 
debates of the Constituent Assembly and thereafter could not be starker.
